name: download_revision
title: Save an old revision

account.description: Which account: a label from list_accounts (its editors section). Empty means the default account.

file_id.description: The file's id, or its URL.

format.description: For a Google file: what to save it as.

save_dir.description: A folder inside the downloads folder.

filename.description: Defaults to the file's name with the revision id.

name: drive_changes
title: What changed since the cursor
description: Every file created, edited, moved, trashed or removed since the cursor, and a new cursor to use next time. Only the delta comes back, so this costs the same whether the Drive holds 20 files or 20,000. Call it again while exhausted is false to drain the backlog.

cursor.description: A cursor from start_drive_cursor or from a previous drive_changes call.

name: edit_comment
title: Edit a comment or reply

account.description: Which account this writes as: a label from list_accounts (its editors section). Required; writes have no default.

name: edit_document_section
title: Replace a section of a Google Doc

Read the section with read_document first and pass its revisionId: the edit is one batch, pinned to that revision. Headings in the new body must be deeper than the section's own. Returns the document's title and the section's size before and after, in characters of markdown.

account.description: Which account this writes as: a label from list_accounts (its editors section). Required; writes have no default.

document_id.description: The document's id, or its URL.

section.description: The section's id, path or unique heading title, from read_document.

markdown.description: Markdown: # headings, paragraphs, - and 1. lists (nested by indent), **bold**, *italic*, ~~strike~~, `code`, ``` fences, [links](url), | tables |.

expected_revision.description: The revisionId read_document returned for the text this replaces. The edit is refused if the document has changed since.

clear.description: With an empty markdown: delete everything under the heading.

drop_hidden.description: Delete the images, footnotes and the like the section holds along with its text.

tab.description: A tab other than the first: its id (t.abc) or title, from get_document. Empty means the first tab.

name: editors_api_reference
title: Docs, Sheets and Slides API reference
description: What a Google Docs, Sheets or Slides batchUpdate request takes, from the API's own schema (the revision batch_update_document, batch_update_spreadsheet and batch_update_presentation check against): each field's type, allowed values and meaning, with the types it refers to expanded `depth` levels down (`more` lists the rest by name). Name a request kind (updateTextStyle, repeatCell, createShape) or any type (TextStyle, CellFormat, PageElementProperties); with no name, every request kind and its one-line summary. Kinds marked Developer Preview need the Cloud project in Google's preview program.

name.description: A request kind or a type name. Empty lists the request kinds.

depth.description: How many levels of referred types to expand.

name: fill_placeholders
title: Fill {{tags}} in a deck
description: Replace every {{tag}} with its value (exact case) across the deck, or only the slides named. Reports how many of each were found.

account.description: Which account this writes as: a label from list_accounts (its editors section). Required; writes have no default.

presentation_id.description: The presentation's id, or its URL.

slide_ids.description: Slide object ids (read_deck) to limit it to. Empty means every slide.

name: find_files
title: Search Drive
description: Search the whole Drive without listing it. Combine any of name_contains, full_text, mime_type, parent_id and modified_after; they are ANDed. This is the tool to reach for instead of walking folders, or a local copy of the Drive, which costs a full tree scan for the same answer.

full_text.description: Search inside document contents, Google's own index.

parent_id.description: Restrict to one folder's direct children.

modified_after.description: RFC 3339; a bare date means midnight UTC.

name: find_in_document
title: Find text in a Google Doc
description: Every place a text appears in one tab of a Google Doc (body, headers, footers and footnotes unless segments is body), as ranges [startIndex, endIndex) to use in batch_update_document (with tabId and, outside the body, segmentId), each with its paragraph's range and named style. Returns the revisionId the ranges are right for. With regex, text is a JavaScript regular expression (run under a time limit); a match never crosses a paragraph.

account.description: Which account: a label from list_accounts (its editors section). Empty means the default account.

document_id.description: The document's id, or its URL.

tab.description: A tab's id (t.0) or its title. Empty means the first tab.

regex.description: text is a regular expression, e.g. "\{\{[a-z_]+\}\}" for placeholders.

name: find_people
title: Find people
description: Find a person's email address by name, across every account at once: each account's contacts, the addresses Gmail saved from mail it sent or received ('other'), and a Workspace domain's directory. The query matches the start of a name, an address, a phone number or an organisation. One entry per person, merged by address, with every account and source it was found in; a source an account cannot read is listed under `unavailable` with the reason. Use it before addressing a draft or an invitation to someone named.

query.description: A name or its start ("Ana Pop"), or the start of an address or a phone number.

account.description: Which account: a label from list_accounts, or "*" for every account at once (the default).

sources.description: Where to look: "contacts", "other" (saved from mail) and "directory" (Workspace). Default all three.

limit.description: Per account and source, before merging.

name: find_time
title: Find time
description: Candidate slots of `duration_minutes` across EVERY account (and optional `attendees`), inside working hours (default Mon-Fri 09:00-18:00 UTC), after a minimum notice, clear of existing events plus buffers, on a step grid, ranked earliest first or with mornings/afternoons first. Returns `slots` (overlapping candidates, e.g. 09:00 and 09:30 for an hour) and `ranges` (the free stretches they come from). Tentative events block time unless `tentative_is_free`. If some busy time could not be read, `complete` is false and `unknown` says what.

from.description: YYYY-MM-DD or a time. Empty means today (UTC).

to.description: Exclusive end. Empty means `days` after from.

days.description: Window length when `to` is empty; at most 62.

account.description: Which account: a label from list_accounts, or "*" for every account at once (the default).

calendars.description: "selected" (what the Calendar app shows, the default), "primary" (each account's own calendar only), "all", or a list of calendar ids or names.

attendees.description: Other people's addresses whose free/busy an account may see (colleagues in the same organisation, anyone who shared their calendar). Needs the calendar.events.freebusy scope; without it they are listed under `unknown` and the accounts' own calendars still count.

working_days.description: Days a slot may fall on, in the working-hours zone.

hours_end.description: Working hours end, HH:MM local, exclusive; 24:00 is midnight. After hours_start.

time_zone.description: IANA zone for the working hours, the window and the answer. Empty means the server's zone (UTC).

min_notice_minutes.description: No slot starts sooner than this from now.

buffer_before_minutes.description: Free time kept before each existing event.

buffer_after_minutes.description: Free time kept after each existing event.

step_minutes.description: Slots start on this grid from hours_start: 30 gives :00 and :30.

prefer.description: Rank: earliest first, or that half of the day (before/after 12:00 local) first.

tentative_is_free.description: Offer slots over tentative events and "maybe" answers.

name: format_range
title: Format a range
description: Number format, bold/italic, colours, alignment, wrapping, borders and frozen rows/columns for a range. Only what is given changes.

account.description: Which account this writes as: a label from list_accounts (its editors section). Required; writes have no default.

spreadsheet_id.description: The spreadsheet's id, or its URL.

range.description: A1 range, e.g. "Sheet1!A1:D20", "B:B" or "2:2". No sheet name means the first sheet.

freeze_rows.description: Rows frozen at the top of the range's sheet.

name: forward
title: Forward
description: Forward a message WITH its attachments, under Gmail's 'Forwarded message' block, with an optional note above it (body_text / body_html). Creates a DRAFT unless send is true. Extra attachments can be added.

include_attachments.description: Carry the original's attachments. Default true. The images its body shows travel either way.

to.description: Recipients. Each entry is an address, "Name <address>", or a comma-separated list of those.

cc.description: Cc recipients. Each entry is an address, "Name <address>", or a comma-separated list of those.

bcc.description: Bcc recipients (kept on a draft, stripped from what recipients see). Each entry is an address, "Name <address>", or a comma-separated list of those.

body_text.description: Plain-text body: write paragraphs as single lines, never hard-wrapped. Given alone, an HTML alternative with the same lines is generated, so Gmail renders it as ordinary prose.

body_html.description: HTML body. Given alone, a plain-text alternative is generated from it; give both to control each.

attachments.description: Files to attach. Never type or paste a file's base64 yourself: a retyped file can arrive changed. Copy the file into /srv/inbox/google and give its path, or have a script that read the file send content_base64 with its sha256. The result lists each attachment's sha256 and size: compare them with the source.

path.description: a file in /srv/inbox/google (copy it there with cp; a bare name is taken from /srv/inbox/google). Links are refused. Exactly one of path or content_base64.

content_base64.description: The bytes as standard base64, only as a script that read the file wrote them, never typed. Needs sha256 and filename.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the source file, as sha256sum prints it. Required with content_base64, checked with path; a mismatch fails as checksum_mismatch and nothing is sent.

mime_type.description: Defaults to a guess from the extension.

from.description: Send as this address. It must be one of the account's verified send-as aliases; defaults to the account's default.

send.description: false (default) saves a DRAFT and returns its webUrl. true SENDS immediately. SENDING IS OUTWARD-FACING AND CANNOT BE UNDONE: only send when the user has explicitly approved THIS message (its recipients and its text) in the current conversation. Otherwise create a draft and give the user its webUrl.

account.description: Which mailbox this writes to or sends from: a label from list_accounts. Required; there is no default for writes.

name: free_busy
title: Free/busy
description: When the user is busy across EVERY account in a window, per calendar, plus one merged, de-duplicated `busy` timeline that also covers any `attendees`. Busy means: not cancelled, not "show as available", not declined; tentative events and "maybe" answers count as busy and are flagged `tentative`; an all-day event left as busy blocks its whole day. Anything that could not be read is listed under `unknown` and `complete` is false.

from.description: YYYY-MM-DD or a time. Empty means today (UTC).

to.description: Exclusive end. Empty means `days` after from.

days.description: Window length when `to` is empty; at most 62.

account.description: Which account: a label from list_accounts, or "*" for every account at once (the default).

calendars.description: "selected" (what the Calendar app shows, the default), "primary" (each account's own calendar only), "all", or a list of calendar ids or names.

name: get_attachment
title: Download attachment
description: Download one attachment to disk by message_id + attachment_id (both come from get_thread). This is the capability Google's own Gmail MCP server does not have: it reports an attachment's name and id and gives you no way to fetch the bytes. Returns the path, size and sha256; a download whose size differs from the one Gmail reports for the part is refused and nothing is saved. A different file already saved under the name is kept, and this one is saved as "name (2).ext".

save_dir.description: A folder INSIDE the account's attachments folder (e.g. "2026-09/invoices"); empty for the folder itself. Copy files from the result's path to where they belong.

filename.description: Defaults to <attachment_id>.bin. Path separators are stripped.

account.description: Which registered mailbox: a label from list_accounts; empty means the default account.

name: get_document
title: Read a Google Doc's structure
description: A Google Doc's structure with the indices batch_update_document needs: every tab, and for one tab its body as elements (paragraphs with named style, heading id, bullet, styled runs and objects such as images or footnote marks; tables with each cell's range and content; section breaks; tables of contents), each with range [startIndex, endIndex). A paragraph's `text` holds one U+FFFC per non-text index, so offset k of text is index range[0]+k; its newline is range[1]-1. Styles are shown short ("11pt", "#1a73e8"); in requests write {magnitude: 11, unit: "PT"} and {color: {rgbColor: {red, green, blue}}} (0 to 1). `parts` adds headers, footers, footnotes, lists, named ranges, objects (image sizes and sources) and styles (page setup, named styles); `notShown` says what exists beyond them. A long body is cut at an element (`nextIndex`: read on with start_index). format raw returns the API's JSON, narrowed by `fields`. Returns revisionId for expected_revision. For prose, read_document's markdown is cheaper.

account.description: Which account: a label from list_accounts (its editors section). Empty means the default account.

document_id.description: The document's id, or its URL.

tab.description: A tab's id (t.0) or its title. Empty means the first tab.

parts.description: What to include for the tab.

start_index.description: Only body elements that end after this index.

end_index.description: Only body elements that start before this index.

suggestions.description: How suggested edits show: inline with their ids, as if accepted, or as if rejected. Default: Docs' choice for the account's access.

fields.description: format raw only: a field mask over the Document, e.g. "revisionId,tabs(tabProperties)".

name: get_draft
title: Get draft

account.description: Which registered mailbox: a label from list_accounts; empty means the default account.

name: get_event
title: Get event

account.description: Which account: a label from list_accounts; empty means the default account.

calendar_id.description: Calendar id, from list_calendars or from an agenda event's calendarId. "primary" is the account's own.

'text' (default) adds the attachment list plus each body as readable text, CONVERTING a message that ships only HTML rather than dumping markup; each message carries bodySource so you know which you got. account.description: Which registered mailbox: a label from list_accounts; empty means the default account.

name: get_presentation

No cell data (get_values, read_rows). format raw returns the API's JSON for `ranges`, with grid data if asked, narrowed by `fields`: the way to read cell formats, notes, validation and pivots.

max_threads.description: Threads scanned. Page with the query.

name: health
title: Health
description: Check that every grant is alive, per product and per account. Under `gmail`, per grant: the mailbox each credential resolves to, the scope Google actually GRANTED (not the one credentials.json declares), whether it can write, and the OAuth client the live token belongs to; an account may hold its own gmail.modify grant and a gmail.readonly one, and `activeGrant` is the one the tools use. Under `calendar`: that the grant refreshes, which account it resolves to (the consent screen offers every account signed in), and whether it carries the scopes the tools need. Under `drive`: which account the grant acts as and the storage used. Under `editors` (Docs, Sheets, Slides), per account: the address, the granted scopes, and whether each of the three APIs is enabled in the grant's Cloud project. Under `tasks`, `contacts` and `meet`, per account with a grant: the address, the granted scopes, and whether the API answers (`disabled` when its Cloud project has not enabled it); contacts also says which sources it reads. Checks EVERY account by default. Run this before concluding the server is broken, and before retrying a write that refused.

account.description: Which account: a label from list_accounts, or "*" for every account (the default).

name: link_sheet_cells
title: Link existing text cells
description: Add or replace hyperlinks on existing plain text cells in one atomic batch. Keeps their values, validation and all other formatting. Row and column are 1-based. Every cell must still contain expected_text; formulas, rich text and chips are refused before any write.

account.description: Which account this writes as: a label from list_accounts (its editors section). Required; writes have no default.

spreadsheet_id.description: The spreadsheet's id, or its URL.

name: list_accounts

Under `gmail`: the mailboxes, which one a tool uses when no account is given, and which grant each runs on: `modify` (its own; the write tools work) or `readonly` (a read-only grant; the write tools refuse). Under `calendar`: the accounts whose calendars it reaches, the address each grant must resolve to, and the time zone. Under `drive`: which grant Drive runs on (its own once begin_consent made one, else an rclone remote's when one is configured). Under `editors`: the accounts Docs, Sheets and Slides can act as (one may run on the Drive grant; any other needs a grant made with begin_consent). Under `tasks`, `contacts` and `meet`: the accounts with a grant for Google Tasks, for contacts and the directory, and for Meet's records. Says nothing about whether a grant is alive; that is health, which costs a round trip to Google.

name: list_calendars
title: List calendars
description: Every calendar each account can see (its own, shared ones, subscriptions, holidays), with its id, the account's access to it, and whether agenda reads it by default.

account.description: Which account: a label from list_accounts, or "*" for every account at once (the default).

name: list_comments
title: List a file's comments

account.description: Which account: a label from list_accounts (its editors section). Empty means the default account.

file_id.description: The file's id, or its URL.

name: list_drafts

account.description: Which registered mailbox: a label from list_accounts; empty means the default account.

name: list_labels

value_input.description: USER_ENTERED parses as if typed ("=SUM(A:A)" a formula, "2026-10-08" a date, "12.5" a number); RAW stores strings as text.

include_values.description: Return the written cells as Sheets now renders them.

name: upload_file
title: Upload a file to Drive
description: Put a file on Drive byte for byte and prove it: after the upload, Drive's own checksum of what it stored (or the bytes read back, when Drive reports none) is compared with the source's. A difference fails the call and is taken back: a replacement's damaged revision is deleted, a new file is trashed. The file goes as path (a file in /srv/inbox/google (copy it there with cp; a bare name is taken from /srv/inbox/google)) or as content_base64 with its sha256. Never type or paste a file's base64 yourself: a retyped file can arrive changed. Copy the file into /srv/inbox/google and give its path, or have a script that read the file send content_base64 with its sha256. The folder is folder_id, else folder_path, else the root. A name already in the folder is refused unless if_exists says what to do. A file given by path keeps its modification time on Drive. Returns the stored file with its link, size, sha256, md5 and verifiedBy. With convert, an Office file (.docx, .doc, .xlsx, .xls, .csv, .pptx, .ppt) becomes a Google Doc, Sheet or deck instead, named without its extension; a converted file keeps no bytes to compare, so the check is that Drive made the Google type, and the result gives the source's size and sha256 under `source`.

path.description: The file as a file in /srv/inbox/google (copy it there with cp; a bare name is taken from /srv/inbox/google). Links are refused.

content_base64.description: The bytes as standard base64, only as a script that read the file wrote them, never typed. Needs sha256 and filename.

sha256.description: Hex SHA-256 of the source file. Required with content_base64, checked with path.

folder_id.description: The destination folder's id. Takes precedence over folder_path.

folder_path.description: The destination folder's path under My Drive; empty is the root.

filename.description: The name on Drive; defaults to the file's (the same key a Gmail attachment takes).

mime_type.description: Defaults to a guess from the name.

if_exists.description: A file of that name already there: "fail" (default), "replace" (new revision, same id), or "keep_both".

convert.description: Upload an Office file as the Google Doc, Sheet or deck it converts to. Default false: the bytes as they are.

name: upsert_rows
title: Upsert rows by key
description: Update the rows whose `key` column matches (only the columns given change), append the rest. One atomic batch. A key on two sheet rows is refused.

account.description: Which account this writes as: a label from list_accounts (its editors section). Required; writes have no default.

spreadsheet_id.description: The spreadsheet's id, or its URL.

sheet.description: The sheet (tab) name, from list_sheets. Empty means the first sheet.

header_row.description: The row that names the columns (1-based).

key.description: The header name of the column that identifies a row.

amount.description: An exact decimal string, e.g. "12.50": stored as a number, never through a float you computed.

rows.description: Objects keyed by the header row's names. Numbers and booleans are stored as such, "=..." as a formula, "YYYY-MM-DD" (or with THH:MM) as a date, any other string as text; null clears a cell. A key the header lacks is refused.

name: write_range
title: Write a range
description: Values or formulas into an A1 range that names its sheet ("Invoices!A2:C4"), parsed as if typed (USER_ENTERED): "=SUM(B2:B9)" is a formula, "28/09/2026" a date in the sheet's locale. Returns `before`, what those cells held (formulas as formulas), so the write can be undone by writing it back.

account.description: Which account this writes as: a label from list_accounts (its editors section). Required; writes have no default.

spreadsheet_id.description: The spreadsheet's id, or its URL.

range.description: A1 range with its sheet, e.g. "Sheet1!A1:D20".

values.description: Rows of cells, top to bottom.
